evidence_inputs: The node adds a final pass to detect_signal_sources: grouped_ids is the union of the multi-group member ids, and every signal in the fetch result not in that set becomes a one-member group keyed by its accessor (falling back to its id when accessor is null). The pass routes every group through the function's own MERGE, so the min_instances threshold is unchanged: a two-member pattern forms no shared group and each of its signals gets its own source. The unused create_signal_source was deleted from imas_codex/discovery/base/grouping.py. Two commits: b90e7fd275a6e1121b87023d86473d042d4ceda3 (code + tests) and 1b8457bbf16b057141a52193b629e5cab20d16d3 (evidence fragment). Callers: the only consumer of the return value is parallel.py:5098 and the enrich-loop progress callback, both logging-only, so widening groups_detected to include singletons changes no control flow. claim_signals_for_enrichment excludes a signal only when it is MEMBER_OF a source whose representative_id differs, so a one-member source's signal (its own representative) is claimed, as the plan intends. The graph test builds facility pytest-singleton-<12hex>, two ungrouped signals (ALPHA_ONLY, BETA_ONLY) plus one three-member pattern (TRIP_00N:V), and asserts (3,5); a re-run returns (0,0); a second-run count query shows 3 sources and 5 edges; after propagate_source_enrichment the source reads enriched and claim_sources_for_candidates(facility) returns it; all fixture nodes are removed in a finally block. The plan's literal done-when grep `grep -rn create_signal_source imas_codex/ tests/` does NOT print nothing at the reviewed head: it matches 8 lines of the unrelated symbol detect_and_create_signal_sources in mdsplus/graph_ops.py and static/workers.py; the manifest honestly records the word-boundary form `grep -rnw`, which is empty.

findings.text: follow-on: evidence: the plan's node done-when states `grep -rn create_signal_source imas_codex/ tests/ prints nothing`, but at the reviewed head that command prints 8 lines — all from the distinct symbol detect_and_create_signal_sources (mdsplus/graph_ops.py:455, static/workers.py, tests/discovery/test_static_parallel.py). The manifest's evidence_inputs correctly substitutes `grep -rnw`, which is empty, and the plan text itself says detect_and_create_signal_sources serves MDSplus SignalNodes and is left alone, so the intent (the deleted creator has no references) holds. But the literal check as written is not met, and neither the manifest nor the fragment says why the substitution was needed. Fix: correct the plan's grep to a word-boundary form, or record in the fragment that create_signal_source survives only as a substring of the unrelated detect_and_create_signal_sources.

follow-on: fit: the bulk channel-element skip in claim_signals_for_enrichment guards on `AND NOT EXISTS { (s)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(:SignalSource) }`. Before this change every ungrouped signal had no source, so a channel-like sub-threshold signal (accessor matching e.g. `.*[_:]\d{2,3}\)?$`) was bulk-marked skipped; after the change every such signal owns a one-member source, the guard is false, and the signal is claimed for individual LLM enrichment instead. This is the plan's stated intent (each one-member source's representative is enriched so the signal can reach the map), not a defect, but the interaction with the channel-element optimisation is unmentioned in the fragment and uncovered by the graph test (whose singletons are ALPHA_ONLY/BETA_ONLY, both non-numeric). Fix: state the interaction in the fragment and quantify the extra enrichments for JT-60SA, or add a channel-like singleton to the fixture.

follow-on: durability: four mocked tests cover the singleton pass but none exercises the null-accessor branch — the line `key = r["accessor"] if r["accessor"] is not None else r["id"]`. A signal with accessor null is skipped out of pattern_groups, is not in grouped_ids, and is therefore sourced alone keyed by its id; that path is unreachable in the suite. Add a case whose result carries accessor=None and assert group_key and group_id fall back to the signal id.

follow-on: durability: the mocked tests locate the shared versus singleton MERGE calls with `_merge_calls` + a member_count dict and with `call_args_list[1]` in test_signals_pipeline.py, so they pin call order and count rather than the pass's set of group keys. They would not catch a regression that emitted the right (groups, members) totals with the wrong keying. The live graph test does assert member_count 1,1,3 and the (0,0) second run, which is the stronger evidence.

follow_ons: plan §3 node done-when should state the grep with a word boundary (or explain the unrelated detect_and_create_signal_sources substring); the fragment should record the channel-element-skip interaction with one-member sources and its enrichment cost; add a null-accessor singleton case to tests/discovery/test_singleton_sources.py; the manifest carries no canonical baseline_suite/after_suite JSON, so the added-failure count is only recoverable by re-running the arms (done here).
